Summary of technical feasibility and caveats:

Short answer: 99.995% is feasible but only under Dedicated (reserved capacity) with active-active across 2 US regions, aggressive redundancy, and dedicated priority routing. The latency band (P95 < 220ms) is plausible inside a region; cross-region P95 will be higher and depends on customer location and network egress.

Detailed notes:
- Availability: Achieve via 3 active nodes per shard in two regions, health-based auto-failover, and faster warm-start of replicas. We'll need to pin model variants and KV caches to avoid cold starts.
- Latency: To meet p50/p95 we must:
  - deploy cross-region KV replication to keep caches warm (adds write amplification and infra cost)
  - reserve network egress paths and limit burst concurrency per tenant
- Operational: requires new SRE runbooks, 24/7 oncall escalation for that route, and a dedicated support alias (we can use redwood-enterprise-support@redwood.com).
- Estimated infra delta: ~$18k–$25k/month for cross-region reserved capacity and replication overhead for the requested traffic profile.
- Engineering effort: ~6 weeks to implement priority routing, KV replication & rollout checklist; ~2 weeks additional for full validation and playbook docs.

I'm attaching a short infra-impact summary that lays out failure modes and mitigations. If the commercial team wants our SLA to include latency across all customer geos, the cost and time go up considerably.

Marcus Lin
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference
Attachment: infra-impact-summary.pdf
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Custom SLA ask: 99.995% uptime + latency commitments for Velari Prod

Appreciate the notes Marcus — a proposed product-facing approach to limit risk and speed delivery:

Proposal (staged SLA):
1) Stage 1 (pilot, 0-90 days): provide 99.95% uptime commitment with target latency bands (P50 < 75ms, P95 < 300ms) while we validate workloads and traffic shapes. Use Dedicated reserved capacity with priority routing but no cross-region replication.
2) Stage 2 (post-stabilization, after 90 days): upgrade to 99.995% and tightened latency (P50 < 60ms, P95 < 220ms) conditional on observed error/latency distributions and completion of KV replication + additional infra.

Controls and rollout:
- Canary traffic routing and automatic rollback hooks.
- Instrumented evals with Velari prompt set for quality and latency regressions.
- Monthly SLO reports and a 30-day refinement window before Stage 2 goes live.

This reduces upfront infra spend, gives Velari an earlier SLA commitment they can use internally, and gives our engineering team a deterministic path to the higher SLO. From product side, this is our recommended path.

Dev Patel
Product Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
